newsitem.title: UK: UKCont/west tanker rates firm, more sails west.
newsitem.headline: UKCont/west tanker rates firm, more sails west.

text.p: Large tanker rates for westwards routes from the North Sea were steady to firm on Monday as more charterers picked up tonnage for the voyage, shipping brokers said.

Million-barrel vessels were expected to fetch a healthy W110 as bad weather added to good demand for vessels. Sun Oil's fixture of the 136,000 tonne Tromso Confidence at W105 was seen right on the market.
Statoil also fixed a 280,000 tonner from Norway to Canada at W67.5.
Brokers said 260,000 tonne very large crude carriers (VLCCs) making the transatlantic voyage would be worth around W65, perhaps slightly up from last week.
But mideastern routes to Japan were flat as VLCCs continued to trickle eastwards.
Idemitsu's fixtures of a 250,000 tonne Yukong VLCC at W67.5 was in line with the market, which has changed little in the past week.
Rates to the U.S. Gulf for two million barrel vessels were also little changed at around W52.5. "I do not see a reason for these rates to change," a broker said.
West African fixing was quieter than last week, with VLCCs to the U.S. Gulf talked unchanged at around W65.
But fuel oil tanker rates from the Baltics to northwestern European destinations were perky, with at least three trading companies heard looking for fresh vessels.
25,000 tonners were asking between W195 and W210, depending on timing and age. "There is still a bit of interest there which is keeping things up a bit," one dealer said.
Rates in the Med were holding strong too as supplies continue to flow from Novorossiisk.
